subject: french
title: Stamp 3: Immigration Debate
welcome_lead: Stamp the contemporary immigration debate in French society.
meta_desc: A-Level French adventure on the immigration debate, integration, and political parties.

concepts.def: Migration into France; a central issue in contemporary French politics.
Process by which immigrants become part of French society and culture.
Far-right party led by Marine Le Pen, formerly Front National, opposing immigration.
Right of asylum, protecting persecuted persons under the 1951 Geneva Convention.
Granting legal status to undocumented immigrants (sans-papiers).
Numerical limit on immigration; periodically proposed in political debates.

walkthroughs.body_html: France has long welcomed migrants from former colonies (North Africa, sub-Saharan Africa) and other EU countries. Today around 10% of residents are immigrants, sparking heated political debate.

The Rassemblement national calls for strict limits and prioritising native French (preference nationale). The left emphasises welcoming refugees and regularising sans-papiers. The centre seeks managed migration.
Un sans-papiers = undocumented person. Un demandeur d'asile = asylum seeker. Un refugie = refugee. La naturalisation = acquisition of citizenship.
